newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues new rules on mortgage management.
newsitem.headline: China issues new rules on mortgage management.

text.p: China has issued new rules on the management of mortgages that aim to keep order in the nation's erratic real estate markets and protect the rights of lenders and borrowers, the China Securities said on Wednesday.

All mortgaging activities carried out in urban planning areas would have to follow the "Methods of Urban Real Estate Mortgage Management", while mortgages issued in other areas would have to refer to the new rules, the newspaper said.
The regulations, issued by the Ministry of Construction, would come into force on June 1, it said.

Under the rules, land use rights for mortgaged property that was part of unfinished projects would be tied to the mortgage, while mortgages on property bought at state-subsidised prices would be limited, it said.
The period of mortgages issued to enterprises with a fixed lifetime should not exceed that lifetime, nor should the life of a mortgage exceed the period of land-use rights on a property.
Borrowers of mortgages on rented property should inform the tenant about the mortgage and inform the lender about the rent contract, it said.
The rules also covered mortgage signing, registration, management and possession of mortgaged property and the disposal of mortgaged property, it said.
They also laid out the legal responsibilities of borrowers and lenders, the newspaper said but gave no details.

China has moved cautiously in developing a mortgage lending market, despite the need to find ways to finance sales of housing to low-income urban residents and to stabilise the boom-and-bust property market.
Concerns that mortgage lending could trigger another round of real estate speculation and lead to inflationary pressure have added to official caution over mortgage development.
